## Open findings

Raised by the documentation itself, in part 7 of each model chapter and of D6, the pricing
tool's chapter. Each has a compensating control and an owner, and each row is the chapter's
own, word for word.

### D4 Business Credit Score

From [D4.7](score/limitations.qmd).

| # | Finding | Evidence | Compensating control | Owner | Status |
|--|--------------|----------------|------------------|-------|------|
| 1 | No out-of-time sample: origination is a single cross-section, so temporal stability is untested. | Train and test are random splits of one cohort; PSI between them ({{< var score.psi_score >}} on the score) measures sampling noise, not drift. | Monitoring plan (D4.8): score and feature PSI on each new cohort, with redevelopment triggers. | Model developer | open |
| 2 | The gate population is not the lending population. | Held-out AUC {{< var score.pop.everyone.auc >}} on all applicants (the gate, {{< var score.gate >}}); {{< var score.pop.booked.auc >}} on the booked only. | Report both on every run; track the booked-only AUC beside the gate; consider gating on the booked population at redevelopment. | Model developer | open |
| 3 | Features with no causal role in the generator are in the model (`industry`, `entity_type`, `trade_lines`). | Together they carry {{< var score.var_share_structural >}} of the logit's variance on the held-out applicants. | Present but inert: remove at the next redevelopment; removal is a simplification, not a risk fix. | Model developer | open |
| 4 | The score distribution is concentrated in one band. | {{< var score.band.D.n >}} of {{< var score.n_test >}} held-out applicants ({{< var score.band_d_share >}}) fall in band D, limiting discrimination inside it. | Downstream decisions use the PD, not the band alone; review band boundaries at redevelopment. | Model developer | open |
| 5 | The weight of evidence of `leverage` is not monotonic, although the generator's effect of leverage is. | Read in bin order, WoE is not monotonic in {{< var score.woe_nonmonotonic >}}; `monotonic_trend` is left at optbinning's `"auto"` default. | Set `monotonic_trend` explicitly for each numeric feature at the next redevelopment and re-verify the gate; until then, discrimination is unaffected, since every performance figure is measured with these bins. | Model developer | open |
| 6 | The model under-predicts default risk in band B on the booked population. | Observed / predicted {{< var score.band_booked.B.ratio >}} on the held-out booked in band B, outside the {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}}–{{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}} tolerance, on {{< var score.band_booked.B.defaults >}} defaults (the monitoring floor is {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}}). | Recalibrate band B, or apply a calibration overlay to it, at the next review; until then, monitor booked band B's observed / predicted on each cohort against the floor. | Model developer | open |

### D5 Loan Adjudication

From [D5.7](adjudication/limitations.qmd).

| # | Finding | Evidence | Compensating control | Owner | Status |
|--|--------------|----------------|------------------|-------|------|
| 1 | On the loans the bank books, held-out AUC is below the AUC gate value, and no better than the scorecard the model consumes. | Held-out AUC {{< var adj.pop.everyone.auc >}} on all applicants (the gate, {{< var adj.gate_auc >}}); {{< var adj.pop.booked.auc >}} on the booked only (bootstrap 95% interval {{< var adj.pop.booked.auc_ci_lo >}}–{{< var adj.pop.booked.auc_ci_hi >}}, wholly below the gate), against the scorecard's {{< var score.pop.booked.auc >}} on the same rows (paired difference {{< var adj.vs_score.booked.diff >}}, interval {{< var adj.vs_score.booked.lo >}} to {{< var adj.vs_score.booked.hi >}}). Lift on the booked, {{< var adj.pop.booked.lift >}}×, still clears its {{< var adj.gate_lift >}}× gate. | Report both populations on every run; track the booked-only AUC and lift beside the gates; at redevelopment, weigh gating on the booked population and placing the zones on the scorecard's PD instead. | Model developer | open |
| 2 | Two policy rules can never fire on this data: the leverage cap and the request-to-revenue cap. | Leverage cap {{< var adj.policy.leverage_cap >}} against a largest leverage of {{< var adj.max_leverage >}}; request-to-revenue cap {{< var adj.policy.req_to_rev_cap >}} against a largest ratio of {{< var adj.max_req_to_rev >}}; {{< var adj.rule.leverage.n_all >}} and {{< var adj.rule.large_request.n_all >}} hits over all {{< var adj.n_applicants >}} applicants. | Treat both as untested controls: restate each limit on this data's definition of its ratio, or remove it, at the next policy review; until then, monitor every rule's hit rate and flag any rule with no hits. | Credit policy owner | open |
| 3 | The Approve zone under-predicts default, on the held-out booked and on all held-out applicants. | Observed / predicted in the Approve zone {{< var adj.zone.booked.Approve.ratio >}} on the held-out booked ({{< var adj.zone.booked.Approve.defaults >}} defaults) and {{< var adj.zone.everyone.Approve.ratio >}} on all held-out applicants ({{< var adj.zone.everyone.Approve.defaults >}} defaults), outside the {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}}–{{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}} tolerance (the monitoring floor is {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}}). | Calibrate the PD at the next retrain, then recalibrate the zones; until then, monitor the Approve zone's observed / predicted on each cohort against the floor, and never read the PD as a default rate. | Model developer | open |
| 4 | The PD-zone cutoffs are set as quantiles over all applicants, held-out rows included. | `t_low` {{< var adj.t_low >}} and `t_high` {{< var adj.t_high >}} from all {{< var adj.n_applicants >}} applicants; from the training rows' in-sample PDs alone, {{< var adj.trainonly.t_low >}} and {{< var adj.trainonly.t_high >}}, which change {{< var adj.trainonly.changed >}} of {{< var adj.n_test >}} held-out decisions. | Take the cutoffs from training rows only, preferably from out-of-sample PDs, at the next retrain. Immaterial in effect today: no interim action beyond this record. | Model developer | open |
| 5 | The lift gate's function is named `top_ventile_lift` but measures the top {{< var adj.lift_top_share >}}. | Measured on the function, its top group is {{< var adj.lift_top_share >}} of the rows, not a twentieth; the module docstring, the validation report, the metadata key and `verify.py` all call it `top-20%` lift. | Rename the function at the next change to `train.py`. The number is right and the gate is unaffected; until then, this record is the control. | Model developer | open |
| 6 | On held-out booked loans, the Decline zone over-predicts default. | Observed / predicted {{< var adj.zone.booked.Decline.ratio >}} in the Decline zone on the held-out booked, on {{< var adj.zone.booked.Decline.defaults >}} defaults among {{< var adj.zone.booked.Decline.n >}} files, outside the {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}}–{{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}} tolerance (the monitoring floor is {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}}); inside it on all held-out applicants ({{< var adj.zone.everyone.Decline.ratio >}}). | Monitor and explain, do not recalibrate: track the booked Decline zone's observed / predicted on each cohort against the floor, and read it as a selection effect unless the all-applicant ratio moves too. | Model developer | open |

### D6 Pricing

From [D6.7](pricing/limitations.qmd). Pricing is a tool, not a model (D0); its findings are
about what its output means, what is untested and who governs its inputs.

| # | Finding | Evidence | Compensating control | Owner | Status |
|--|--------------|----------------|------------------|-------|------|
| 1 | The headline mispricing share measures the data generator's quotes, not a pricing practice. | The generator quotes each loan at break-even on its true PD plus `base_margin` ({{< var market.base_margin >}}), with no capital charge; clearing the hurdle needs the capital charge, {{< var pricing.capital_charge >}}, which exceeds the margin by {{< var pricing.capital_charge_less_margin >}}. A loan clears only where the scorecard's PD sits far enough below the quote's, or the quote's noise covers the gap: {{< var pricing.share_mispriced >}} of the {{< var pricing.n >}} booked loans do not. | Report the mispriced share as a demonstration of the measure on generated quotes, never as a finding about a book, wherever it is shown; before any use on real loans, measure against the bank's actual quoted rates. | Pricing tool owner (proposed; to be named) | open |
| 2 | The tool's summary does not separate loans that lose money from loans that only miss the hurdle. | {{< var pricing.below_break_even.n >}} booked loans ({{< var pricing.below_break_even.share >}}), with \${{< var pricing.below_break_even.ead >}} of EAD, are quoted below break-even and have negative ROE; `portfolio_summary` returns one mispriced flag, its share and mispriced EAD, with no break-even measure, so they are counted among the {{< var pricing.n_mispriced >}} mispriced loans and not shown as such. | Report the below-break-even count and EAD beside the mispriced share (the facts recompute both on every `verify.py` run) and monitor them; add both to `portfolio_summary` at the next change to `pricing/`. | Pricing tool owner (proposed; to be named) | open |
| 3 | In bands AAA to B, the hurdle-clearing and recommended rates rest on a PD that under-predicts default on the booked. | On the held-out booked the scorecard's observed / predicted is {{< var score.band_booked.B.ratio >}} in band B (D4 finding 6) and {{< var score.band_booked.A.ratio >}} and {{< var score.band_booked.AAA.ratio >}} in bands A and AAA (below the floor of {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} defaults); a PD that is too low makes both rates too low. These bands also show the highest mispriced share; read from the generator's code, that concentration comes from finding 1's construction, not from the PD: mispriced share {{< var pricing.band.AAA.mispriced_rate >}} in band AAA and {{< var pricing.band.A.mispriced_rate >}} in band A, against {{< var pricing.best_band_rate >}} in band {{< var pricing.best_band >}}. | Re-run pricing after D4's band-B recalibration; until then, monitor the mispriced share and EAD by band beside D4's band calibration on the booked, and do not set a band's price floor from the recommended rates in bands AAA to B. | Pricing tool owner (proposed; to be named), with the model developer (D4) | open |
| 4 | `fee_rate` can be moved in the workbench but no test sets it, and the book-level functions have no unit tests. | `fee_rate` defaults to {{< var pricing.fee_rate >}} outside `MARKET`; none of the {{< var pricing.n_engine_tests >}} engine tests sets it, yet the v2 what-if accepts it and shows a slider for it. `price_population` and `portfolio_summary` are exercised only through the portal tests, the facts tests and `verify.py`'s comparison with the committed summary. | Add an engine test at a non-zero fee and unit tests of `price_population` and `portfolio_summary` at the next change to `pricing/`; until then, the facts re-check both rate identities at a fee of {{< var pricing.fee_probe >}} on every booked loan on every `verify.py` run ({{< var pricing.identity.fee >}}), which catches the waterfall and the rate solvers disagreeing about the fee, not a fee mishandled the same way in both. The book-level functions have no interim control beyond `verify.py`'s summary comparison. | Pricing tool developer | open |
| 5 | The market assumptions have no owner or change control beyond code review, and the cost of funds alone moves the outcome most. | `MARKET` is a dict in `shared/config.py` with no owner, effective date or change log. A {{< var pricing.sens.step >}} move in `cost_of_funds` takes the share clearing from {{< var pricing.share_clears >}} to {{< var pricing.sens.cost_of_funds.up.share_clears >}} or {{< var pricing.sens.cost_of_funds.down.share_clears >}}, the widest swing of the six assumptions; the same dict sets the generator's quotes and line increase's gate. | Name an owner for each assumption (6.4), keep a dated change log, and re-run 6.5, 6.6 and D8's gate before a change is used; until then, `verify.py` fails on any change to `MARKET` until the facts are rebuilt, and every change is reviewed and recorded as code (D9). | Pricing tool owner, with Treasury and Finance (all proposed; to be named) | open |
